decisions.text: We want it to be a universal remote uh that everyone would want. Um we want to be modern, fun, different. Uh it needs to be sturdy, easy to find, so we gonna have that locator function.
We decided that it should probably be one-handed. Something we could use with one hand.

We decided our remote, uh we want it to be a universal remote uh that everyone would want. Um we want to be modern, fun, different. Uh it needs to be sturdy, easy to find, so we gonna have that locator function.

We decided a universal remote control is actually quite a difficult object to design and possibly within maybe the budget that we do it, um because you'd need to know all the specs of all the electronic companies.
We decided to focus on a T_V_ remote control instead of a universal remote.
We decided to focus on a user-centred design for the remote control, with fewer buttons and simpler to use.
We decided to incorporate the corporate colour (grey and yellow) and our slogan, 'We put the fashion in electronics', on the remote.
We decided not to include teletext functionality.
We decided not to include speech recognition due to cost and practicality concerns, despite younger people's interest.
We decided to include a locator function for the remote, possibly with a holder/charger that also serves as a locator.
We decided to use a minimal number of buttons: 1-9 for channel input, volume up/down, channel up/down, power, mute, and a menu button for additional functions.
We decided to explore a scroll wheel for navigation, possibly with a click function, and to consider ergonomic aspects like a bulge for better grip.
We decided to explore a circular design with buttons around the thumb for a one-handed use, which would work for both left and right-handed users.
We decided to explore a two-piece remote concept: one for quick zapping (channels, volume, power) and another for more detailed functions.
We decided to focus on a specific target group to help determine the remote's design and features.
